text:
matt: Heads-up — observed repeated Xid errors from node gpu-3c2 over the last 30m. ECC single-bit counts creeping up, intermittent nvml reset messages. Pods keeping running but perf is noisy. Need a quick way to pull and correlate kernel/journal + nvidia-smi output to know whether this is HW, driver, or a bad power rail.

jia: can you paste the short log snippet? also which k8s cluster/az?

matt: cluster=prod-us-west2, az=us-west2-b. clipped logs: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00:00): 61, PID=1042, GPU=0: Ch 00000040, 00000000, 00000000
[ 1234.568012] NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568230] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
```
and from nvidia-smi: 
```
GPU  UUID                                 ECC_ERRORS (single)|ECC_ERRORS (double)
0    GPU-abc123def456                     12                   0
```

olga: thanks. first pass checklist: collect persistent journal, dmesg, the last nvidia-smi -q snapshots, and pod logs around the same timestamps. we should also capture HW ids (PCI addr, bus id, GPU UUID) so we can map to inventory.

kevin: +1. to speed this up we should standardize a short parsing pipeline:
- capture kernel lines with Xid or "GPU has fallen off the bus"
- extract Xid code, PCI addr, PID, GPU index
- cross-reference PID -> container via /proc/<pid>/cgroup (or kubectl ps for container id)
- pull last 5 nvidia-smi -q snapshots and ECC counters

jia: here are quick commands to run on the node (one-liners):
```sh
# kernel dmesg slice around recent Xid lines
sudo journalctl -k --since "-45m" | grep -i -E "Xid|GPU has fallen off the bus|NVRM" -n | tail -n 50

# nvml snapshot + ECC counters
sudo nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,FAULT,UTILIZATION,POWER > /tmp/nv-snap-$(date +%s).txt

# map PID -> pod
PID=1042; sudo ls -l /proc/$PID/cgroup || true
```

olga: for automated ingestion we should land two parser rules in our log-shipper: one for kernel/journal and one for nvidia-smi blobs. sample regex for dmesg: 
```regex
^\[\s*([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)\] NVRM: Xid \(([^)]+)\): (\d+), PID=(\d+), GPU=(\d+):\s*(.*)$
```
fields: timestamp_seconds, pci_slot, xid_code, pid, gpu_index, description

matt: that pci_slot capture is key — we can map pci_slot -> chassis & slot in inventory and see if the same physical slot has repeated events.

kevin: also capture the kernel oops/traceback around resets. Xid 61 often is a MM fault; 13 is something else. we should keep a small lookup table in the parser that maps Xid -> likely fault class (eg memory, scheduler, page fault, hw reset).

jia: proposal for journald forwarding (systemd service) to ensure we get persistent GPU lines even after node reboots: 
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Forward GPU kernel logs to collector
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc "journalctl -k --no-pager -o cat --since \"-1h\" | grep -i -E 'NVRM|Xid|GPU has fallen off' | nc log-collector.internal 10514"
```

olga: and for nvidia-smi snapshots we can add a small cron @reboot + on-demand hook in the node agent to call: 
```sh
# node-agent snippet
if sudo nvidia-smi -q > /var/log/nvidia-snap/latest-nv.txt; then curl -XPOST -F file=@/var/log/nvidia-snap/latest-nv.txt https://ingest.internal/gpu-snaps; fi
```

matt: nice. how do we avoid noise/false positives for transient Xid spikes during big batches?

kevin: thresholding: only auto-drain when (Xid_count_last_hour > 5 AND ECC_single_errors > 10) OR (consistent "GPU lost bus" messages). Otherwise create an alert for SRE to triage. we already have a cost/ops impact with auto-drain; draining false positives hurts throughput.

jia: adding correlation step: for each Xid event, try to attach: GPU UUID, PCI slot, pod id, container id, last 3 nvidia-smi snapshots, kernel logs +/- 30s, and node power metrics (if available). Ship all as one envelope so the triage UI can show them together.

olga: sample envelope JSON we should produce (simplified for log-schema team): 
```
{ "gpu_uuid": "GPU-abc123def456", "pci": "0000:af:00.0", "xid": "61", "time": "2025-11-05T02:34:56Z", "pod": "ml-train-42", "nv_snapshots": ["s3://gpu-snaps/..."], "kernel_excerpt": "..." }
```
(we'll implement as flat fields in the index for query speed)

matt: can we also add a quick grep tool in console where engs paste a PID or GPU UUID and it shows correlated lines across sources?

kevin: yes, that will be high ROI. make a small UI that queries our log index with pci/gpu_uuid/pid and time window, then shows related pod info. I'll take a prototype.

sre-bot: Created ISSUE-1892: "GPU log correlation + auto-drain rules" and attached the journal + nvidia-smi snippets from gpu-3c2. Assignee: kevin.

matt: thanks. action items:
- kevin: prototype UI & threshold rule (due EOD Thu)
- olga: add parser regex + journald forwarder PR (due Tue)
- jia: node-agent hook for nv-snap + example one-liners in runbook (today)
- matt: collect additional history for gpu-3c2 and upload to ISSUE-1892 (in progress)

matt: tagging @oncall (just in case) :eyes:

kevin: ack :hammer:

olga: will also add a short runbook note on how to decide drain vs monitor (onepager).

sre-bot: [automated] Reminder: attach hardware mapping data before closing ticket.

matt: will do. thanks all :)
